correctness.rationale: Every legal bipartite residual colouring corresponds to a closed walk of a verified 41-state automaton, with exact deleted-vertex weight. A 41-entry integral reduced-cost potential certifies a universal n/2 lower bound. The only cyclic equality component has verified mod-four advance, excluding equality at n=2 modulo 4. Cyclic concatenations of explicit witness words of lengths 4–8 meet every lower bound. Direct independent brute-force checks confirm n=5–12; finite tests are not substituted for the all-n proof.

evidence: Wei–Li address decycling: destroying all cycles rather than odd cycles; this gives an upper bound on odd-cycle transversal but not equality.
Fox–Gera–Stănică determine maximum independent sets for generalized Petersen graphs; an induced bipartite subgraph is a union of two disjoint independent classes.

Zhu (2009), Theorem 1.4: all eligible triangle-free 2-connected subcubic graphs have induced-bipartite ratio at least 5/7, except Petersen and dodecahedron; this is only a global lower bound, not the claimed exact 3/4-asymptotic periodic value.
Krnc–Pisanski give the condition for the whole graph to be bipartite with no deletions.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The larger graph families studied in these sources come with different optimization constraints. Neither their known statements nor the evaluated implications fix the minimum number of vertices whose removal eliminates odd cycles in GP(n,2).

value.rationale: Exact vertex bipartization for the canonical infinite family GP(n,2) has natural graph optimization meaning and distinguishes odd-cycle elimination from feedback vertex sets. The previously unexplained congruence-2 mod 4 surcharge is structurally explained by a four-layer tight automaton, with an explicit witness for every admissible n; this is neither a parameter rebranding nor an isolated arbitrary calculation.
